QF.id: Analysis of Equity and Debt Instruments_8

question.text: Vikram received 200 bonus shares of a listed company on 15-Aug-2024. The market price on the date of allotment was Rs.500 per share. He sold all bonus shares on 20-Sep-2025 at Rs.650 per share. What is the capital gain and its nature?

answer.text: Rs.30,000 LTCG — holding period includes original shares' holding period
Rs.1,30,000 LTCG — cost is Nil, holding period from allotment date exceeds 12 months
Rs.1,30,000 STCG — bonus shares are always short-term
Rs.30,000 STCG — cost is Rs.500 per share (FMV on allotment date)

explanation.text: The Logic: For bonus shares allotted on or after 01-Apr-2001, the cost of acquisition is NIL. Holding period is counted from the date of allotment (15-Aug-2024), not from the date the original shares were acquired. The period 15-Aug-2024 to 20-Sep-2025 is about 13 months, which exceeds the 12-month threshold for listed equity shares, so the gain qualifies as LTCG. Capital gain = 200 × (Rs.650 - Rs.0) = Rs.1,30,000. The Trap: Option A wrongly uses the FMV on allotment as the cost — for bonus shares the cost is NIL, not the FMV. Option D combines that same FMV-as-cost error with an incorrect short-term classification. Option C is also wrong on the short-term claim — bonus shares are not always short-term; their nature depends on the holding period from allotment. Note: Where these listed bonus shares are sold on a recognised stock exchange with STT paid on the transfer, the resulting LTCG is taxable under section 112A, subject to the prescribed annual exemption limit.
